alex_w: Quick heads-up — ran a kernel-gating sweep on a metal cluster. Observed mis-picks for SM86 vs SM92: short seqs (<=32) are routing to the 'large-block' kernel and KV cache read amplification spikes. Any immediate thoughts?

maria_r: Can you paste the probe flags + a short perf summary?

alex_w: TL;DR: tensor-core BF16 path enabled, FP8 off. On SM86 the runtime chose block-gemm kernel `K_blkA` for seqlen<=32 which regressed p95 latency ~12% on B=1. Throughput unaffected.

jonah_p: Interesting — our selection rule should only enable TensorCoreFP8 when sm_major >= 9. Could the device be misdetected?

sophie_k: What do `nvidia-smi` / device query show?

alex_w: Quick log snippet: 
```json
{"device":0,"sm":86,"driver":"525.85","cap_flags":["tensor_cores","bf16"]}
```
Looks like SM=86 but the selector matched the FP8/TensorCore path anyway.

maria_r: Wait — I remember we had a string-compare bug in the gating code. If you compare '86' >= '9' as strings it can be true depending on implementation. Could be a typo where we left sm version as string.

jonah_p: Yup — seen that before. Code used `if sm_version >= '86'` instead of numeric. That would flip logic for >=9 checks too.

dmitri_s: Also note: when kernel policy switches we currently keep the same `plan_id` for KV cache entries. If the kernel layout changes, reusing plans can cause wrong memory offsets and extra reads. We should invalidate plan entries on kernel-change.

infra-bot: nightly-perf-run: build #4782 reports p95 latency delta +9% on sm86 short-seq bucket. Full results: https://perf.local/build/4782

sophie_k: Proposed action items:
1) Fix sm-version comparison (string -> int) and add unit tests.
2) Bump/derive `plan_id` from `kernel_config` so KV cache is tied to kernel selection.
3) Re-run autotune with explicit seq buckets: [1,16,32,64,128] and reset cached profiles.
4) Add deterministic selection test (input: sm, seqlen, batch -> kernel name).
I'll draft GH issues and PRs.

alex_w: I'll open the numeric-compare PR now. @maria_r can you take the `plan_id` change in runtime?

maria_r: Yep — will add a checksum that mixes `kernel_config` + `kv_cache_version` into the plan id. Also add a migration that invalidates stale entries on rollout.

jonah_p: Suggestion: add a tiny startup probe that logs `cap_flags`, `sm_major`, and a `selector_hash` to runtime logs so we can correlate perf runs in the future (stdout + telemetry tag).

alex_w: Good idea. Will add canary in edge region once PRs land. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

(edited)
